input.question: how do zits form, and why does popping certain zits hurt like a bitch (lip line) and others don't (forehead)
input.ground_truth: There are different kinds of breakout. Whiteheads and blackheads are simply clogged pores; the oil in the pore is either blocked, trapping the bacteria in the pore, or it is exposed to air, where the bacteria oxidizes and forms a whitehead. A pimple, or zit, when the bacteria deeper down in the pore becomes infected and inflamed, and these can be painful. Depending on the location, you can experiences different degrees of pain. There are many more sensitive nerve endings around the lip area, so you feel so many more sensations. That's why kissing someone feels so good, and why cold sores hurt like a mutha.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: how do zits form, and why does popping certain zits hurt like a bitch (lip line) and others don't (forehead)

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your skin is like a soft blanket. Sometimes, your skin gets clogged with tiny bits of dirt, oil, and old skin cells. When these things get stuck in a little hole called a pore, they make a bump called a zit.

Now, some zits are like little water balloons under your skin—they’re squishy but have a strong wall around them. Other zits are closer to the surface and are like bubbles that are almost ready to pop.

When you try to pop a zit on your lip line, that spot has very sensitive skin and is near your mouth, which moves a lot. The skin there is thin and the zit might be deep, so when you try to squeeze it, it hurts a lot—like squishing a balloon that’s stuck in a tight spot!

But zits on your forehead are usually not as deep and the skin there is a bit tougher. So when you try to pop them, it doesn’t hurt as much.

But remember, it’s better not to pop zits at all, because it can make them worse or cause scars! Let your body take care of them, or ask a grown-up for help if you need it.
